changed.title: Five-input monotone f with table 0xeae8e880: some AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 9 gates computes f
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 9 ∧ ∀ x : Fin 5 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = Nat.testBit 0xeae8e880 (∑ i : Fin 5, if x i then 2 ^ (i : ℕ) else 0)
changed.unlocks: settles the least AND/OR size of this five-input monotone function at 9; with the checked row that NOT gates save nothing on it, also its least AND/OR/NOT size
changed.context: FIND (beat this). The answer is an object, not an argument: give the gate list (AND/OR, at most two inputs each, at most 9 gates) and decide the equality over all 32 inputs. The best circuit known to us has 10 gates; none with 8 or fewer exists (exhaustive search, computed, not checked); whether 9 is possible is unknown to us. Pattern: methods/find/example-maj3.lean.txt.
changed.sketch: f on five inputs is true when some listed set is all true: 012, 013, 023, 123, 014, 024, 124, 034 (at least three of 0..3, or 4 with two of 0, 1, 2, or 4 with 0 and 3). We hold a 10-gate AND/OR circuit; an exhaustive search of ours found none with 8 or fewer (computed), so 9 is the only open size. Step: give 9 AND or OR gates, fan-in at most two, each reading only earlier wires, output last; judged by evaluating on all 32 inputs against the table, by decide. A hand idea: share the pair products of 0, 1, 2 between the three-of-four part and the part with 4.
